title: Healing 2.0: Change Your Story, Change Your Life

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When Leon Fleischer was a small child, his older brother took piano lessons.
sentences.zh: 莱昂·弗莱舍很小的时候，他的哥哥在上钢琴课。

sentences.en: The brother didn't much care for them.
sentences.zh: 哥哥对弹钢琴其实并不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: But afterwards, little Leon would climb onto the piano bench and play, note for note,
sentences.zh: 但下课后，小莱昂会爬上琴凳，一个音符不差地弹奏起

sentences.en: the pieces his brother had practiced.
sentences.zh: 哥哥练习过的曲子。

sentences.en: That's when his mother realized Leon was the one who should study the instrument.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他的母亲意识到莱昂才是应该学习钢琴的那个人。

sentences.en: Leon Fleischer made his debut at Carnegie Hall in 1944.
sentences.zh: 莱昂·弗莱舍于1944年在卡内基音乐厅首次登台演出。

sentences.en: He was just 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时年仅16岁。

sentences.en: He performed Brahms' Piano Concerto No.
sentences.zh: 他演奏了勃拉姆斯的《第

sentences.en: 1 in D minor.
sentences.zh: 一号d小调钢琴协奏曲》。

sentences.en: A New York Times music critic said this performance established him
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一位乐评人称赞这次演出确立了他在

sentences.en: as one of the most remarkably gifted of the younger generation of American keyboard artists.
sentences.zh: 美国年轻键盘艺术家中最具非凡天赋的代表之一的地位。

sentences.en: He went on to perform with the world's top orchestras throughout the 1950s and early 60s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代和60年代初，他继续与世界顶尖交响乐团同台演出。

sentences.en: Pause his story here, and Leon Fleischer's life is a triumph.
sentences.zh: 如果把他的故事在这里暂停，莱昂·弗莱舍的人生堪称一场巨大的成功。

sentences.en: But then, something unexpected happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，意想不到的事情发生了。

sentences.en: He started to notice an odd stiffness in his right index finger.
sentences.zh: 他开始注意到自己右手食指有一种奇怪的僵硬感。

sentences.en: His fourth and fifth finger started curling under.
sentences.zh: 他的无名指和小指开始向内蜷曲。

sentences.en: The pain and stiffness grew steadily worse.
sentences.zh: 疼痛和僵硬感持续加剧。

sentences.en: Within a matter of months, his career as a concert pianist was virtually over.
sentences.zh: 短短几个月内，他作为音乐会钢琴家的职业生涯几乎宣告结束。

sentences.en: As you can well imagine, without becoming melodramatic, I was in a very despairing state of depression for about two years.
sentences.zh: 正如你所能想象的那样，并非夸大其词，我在大约两年的时间里陷入了一种极其绝望的抑郁状态。

sentences.en: If we were to take stock of Leon Fleischer's life at this point, we might say it was a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 如果我们此时来审视莱昂·弗莱舍的人生，可能会说这是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: But Leon Fleischer still had so much music in him, so he reinvented himself, becoming a much-admired conductor and teacher.
sentences.zh: 但莱昂·弗莱舍心中依然怀揣着对音乐的热爱，于是他重塑自我，成为了一名备受尊崇的指挥家和老师。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, he continued to try every available measure to heal his right hand.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他继续尝试各种可行的方法来治疗右手。

sentences.en: Eventually, a combination of Botox injections and deep tissue massage started to help.
sentences.zh: 最终，肉毒杆菌注射与深层组织按摩相结合的疗法开始发挥作用。

sentences.en: In 2003, Leon Fleischer made a triumphant return to Carnegie Hall.
sentences.zh: 2003年，莱昂·弗莱舍带着胜利的姿态重返卡内基音乐厅。

sentences.en: He was 75 years old.
sentences.zh: 当时他已经75岁了。

sentences.en: The next year, he released a CD, his first two-handed recording, in over 40 years.
sentences.zh: 第二年，他发行了一张CD，这是他40多年来首次录制双手钢琴专辑。

sentences.en: Today, we kick off a month-long series that we are calling Healing 2.0.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开启一个为期一个月的系列节目，我们称之为“治愈2.0”。

sentences.en: We'll look at the nature of loss and also a mind-bending idea about whether we should try to do away with grief altogether.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨失落的本质，以及一个颠覆常规的想法：我们是否应该彻底消除悲伤？

sentences.en: Plus, we explore whether trauma really does make us stronger and how to craft an apology.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还将探讨创伤是否真的能让我们变得更强大，以及如何得体地道歉。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, how the way we understand the ups and downs of our lives can shape the ups and downs of our lives.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将探讨我们如何理解生活中的起伏，以及这种理解如何塑造我们生活的起伏。

sentences.en: As we make our way through life, it can feel as if we are buffeted by a swiftly moving series of events.
sentences.zh: 在我们走过人生的旅程时，会感觉仿佛被接连不断发生的事态冲击着。

sentences.en: Sometimes, it's all we can do to keep our heads above water as we wait for the next wave to crash over us.
sentences.zh: 有时，我们在等待下一波浪潮将我们淹没时，唯一能做的就是勉强保持清醒。

sentences.en: But research in psychology hints at a different process unfolding beneath the waves,
sentences.zh: 但心理学研究表明，在巨浪之下，还隐藏着另一个正在展开的过程，

sentences.en: an undercurrent that has powerful effects on our well-being, mental health, and life outcomes.
sentences.zh: 一股对我们的幸福感、心理健康和人生结局有着深远影响的潜流。

sentences.en: At Olin College, psychologist Jonathan Adler studies how our minds are shaped by this undercurrent
sentences.zh: 在奥林学院，心理学家乔纳森·阿德尔研究了我们的心灵如何被这股潜流所塑造，

sentences.en: and how becoming mindful of it can help us better deal with setbacks and failure.
sentences.zh: 以及如何意识到这一点能帮助我们更好地应对挫折和失败。

sentences.en: Jonathan Adler, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·阿德尔，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm so excited to be here with you.
sentences.zh: 哦，我很高兴能来到这里与你交流。

sentences.en: Jonathan, I want to take you back to your college days in Maine.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我想带你回到你在缅因州上大学的日子。

sentences.en: You were a capable and hardworking student, but you were also struggling with a secret.
sentences.zh: 你曾是一个能力出众且勤奋的学生，但你也一直在和一个秘密作斗争。

sentences.en: What were you going through?
sentences.zh: 你当时经历了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, like you said, I was a good student.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像你说的，我曾经是个好学生。

sentences.en: I was curious and took classes in a ton of different departments.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，选修了许多不同系别的课程。

sentences.en: But socially, I was more reserved.
sentences.zh: 但在社交方面，我更加内向。

sentences.en: I had a really tight group of friends in high school.
sentences.zh: 我在高中时有一个非常紧密的朋友圈。

sentences.en: And I was sort of angry that that chapter of my life had closed just because high school had ended.
sentences.zh: 我有点生气，仅仅因为高中毕业，我人生中的那个章节就那样结束了。

sentences.en: And I was also struggling with my sexuality, though that's not something I was necessarily conscious of for a big chunk of college.
sentences.zh: 而且我也在跟自己的性取向做斗争，尽管在大学很大一段时间里，我并没有完全意识到这一点。

sentences.en: So you came up with a solution to these challenges, and it was something of a radical solution.
sentences.zh: 所以你为这些挑战想出了一个解决方案，而且是一个相当激进的方案。

sentences.en: What was the plan you devised?
sentences.zh: 你当时制定的计划是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so a lot of students at the college spent part of their junior year studying abroad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，学院里很多学生在大三的时候会选择出国留学一段时间。

sentences.en: And that seemed to me like a rare opportunity to take a break from my regular life and figure out some things about myself.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个难得的机会，可以从日常生活中抽身出来，去理清一些关于我自己的事情。

sentences.en: So I ended up in Perth, which is on the west coast of Australia.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终去了珀斯，它位于澳大利亚西海岸。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which it's literally as far away from my life as you could get.
sentences.zh: 那里的确是我能去到的离我的生活最远的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, if you draw a line from New England through the center of the earth, you end up off the coast of Perth.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你从新英格兰画一条穿过地心的线，你的落点就在珀斯海岸附近。

sentences.en: And this was your way of reinventing yourself?
sentences.zh: 这就是你重塑自我的方式吗？

sentences.en: Well, it felt like an opportunity to step outside my life and sort of explore who I was in a context that wouldn't then have any ramifications for the life that I was living.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这感觉是一个机会，可以跳出我的人生，在一个对我的现实生活不会产生任何后续影响的环境中探索我是谁。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So you fly all the way to Australia.
sentences.zh: 所以你一路飞到了澳大利亚。

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did you find that your social life improved, that you found deep connections with other people?
sentences.zh: 你发现你的社交生活改善了吗？你与其他人建立了深厚的联系吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: When I arrived, I knew that I was going to need to find some friends.
sentences.zh: 当我到达那里时，我知道我需要结交一些朋友。

sentences.en: So I auditioned for the theater department's play.
sentences.zh: 所以我去参加了戏剧系的剧目试镜。

sentences.en: I was studying psychology and theater in college.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里主修心理学和戏剧。

sentences.en: And I knew that being involved in a show was a surefire way to make fast friends and that it also was a place where there might be opportunities to date.
sentences.zh: 我知道参与一场演出是迅速结交朋友的绝佳方法，而且那里也可能会有约会的机会。

sentences.en: And so the play that the department was doing that semester was this weird postmodern adaptation of Chekhov's classic Uncle Vanya by the admittedly brilliant British playwright Howard Barker.
sentences.zh: 因此，该系那个学期排演的剧目是一部对契诃夫经典名作《万尼亚舅舅》的怪诞后现代改编版，出自公认才华横溢的英国剧作家霍华德·巴克之手。

sentences.en: And there's this relatively minor character in the original play, Asterov, who's this brooding intellectual who just thinks but never does anything.
sentences.zh: 在原著中，有一个相对较小的角色叫阿斯特罗夫，他是一个沉郁的知识分子，只会空想却从不付诸行动。

sentences.en: And I figured, oh, that's perfect for me.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，这太适合我了。

sentences.en: But much to my astonishment, I got cast as Vanya, which is one of the only leading roles that I'd ever had.
sentences.zh: 但令我大跌眼镜的是，我竟然被选中饰演万尼亚，这是我演过的为数不多的主角之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So most of Chekhov's plays are about people who are stuck in their lives and sort of consumed with what might have been the joke about Chekhov is that nothing ever happens.
sentences.zh: 契诃夫的大多数戏剧都是关于那些生活停滞不前、某种程度上沉溺于“如果当初”的人们，关于契诃夫有个笑话就是什么事都不会发生。

sentences.en: And so this playwright, Barker, took this play and decided to imagine what would happen if the same characters just did whatever their impulses told them to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这位剧作家巴克拿过这个剧本，决定想象一下，如果这群相同的角色只是凭着自己的冲动行事会发生什么。

sentences.en: So in this version, there are gun battles and unconstrained sex and a whole lot of chaos.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一版中，有枪战、无节制的性爱以及一团混乱。

sentences.en: It's total liberation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种彻底的解放。

sentences.en: And I was an anxious actor.
sentences.zh: 而我当时是个焦虑的演员。

sentences.en: And so having to carry this play in a role that was deeply unsuited to my natural tendencies was all consuming.
sentences.zh: 因此，不得不挑起这部剧的大梁，扮演一个与我天性极其不符的角色，让我耗费了全部的心神。

sentences.en: I had gone looking for the kind of liberation that these characters were given by their playwright.
sentences.zh: 我本是去寻找剧作家赋予这些角色的那种解放。

sentences.en: But in finding it in this fictional world, it completely shut down my own world.
sentences.zh: 但当我在这个虚构的世界里找到它时，它却彻底封闭了我自己的世界。

sentences.en: I felt I had to spend my time mastering this incredibly complex and unnatural language.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我必须把时间花在掌握这种极其复杂且不自然的语言上。

sentences.en: I mean, the first line of the play is just the word uncle repeated over and over.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，剧的第一句台词就是不断重复“舅舅”这个词。

sentences.en: And I just lost all the bandwidth for everything else.
sentences.zh: 我简直失去了处理其他任何事情的精神带宽。

sentences.en: It ended up being one of the loneliest periods of my life with me actually starting to count down the days until I could come home.
sentences.zh: 这最终成了我一生中最孤独的时期之一，我甚至开始倒计时，盼着自己能快点回家。

sentences.en: And what I had envisioned as a time for freedom and exploration actually became this burdened, lonely time.
sentences.zh: 我原本设想中充满自由和探索的时光，实际上却变成了这段充满负担、孤独的岁月。

sentences.en: And I think it set me back in the process of coming out.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它让我出柜的进程倒退了。

sentences.en: So you returned to Maine after the semester abroad.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个学期的海外交换结束后，你回到了缅因州。

sentences.en: You're back now in the same college where you were previously frustrated.
sentences.zh: 你现在回到了曾经让你感到挫败的同一所大学。

sentences.en: What goes through your head at this point?
sentences.zh: 你当时脑子里在想些什么？

sentences.en: I think I felt profoundly disappointed in myself for not having capitalized on this rare opportunity and stifled to be back in my old life without having figured anything out.
sentences.zh: 我想我对自己感到极度失望，因为没有抓住这个难得的机会，而且在什么都没搞懂的情况下又回到了老路上，这让我感到窒息。

sentences.en: And yeah, so I think I just sort of put my head down and kept doing what I knew how to do, which was be a brain, not a fully integrated body.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想我只是有些沮丧地埋头继续做我擅长的事，那就是当一个只用大脑思考、却缺乏完整身心融合的人。

sentences.en: Jonathan's time in Australia felt like more than a misadventure.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森在澳大利亚的经历感觉不仅仅是一次不顺利的冒险。

sentences.en: It felt like a sign.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像是一个征兆。

sentences.en: He had made the trip with high hopes, hoping to become a new person.
sentences.zh: 他怀揣着崇高的愿望踏上旅程，希望成为一个崭新的人。

sentences.en: When he returned no different than before, it didn't just feel the same.
sentences.zh: 当他归来时与以往毫无二致时，这种感觉不仅仅是如出一辙。

sentences.en: It felt worse.
sentences.zh: 它感觉更糟了。

sentences.en: Many of us have had experiences similar to Jonathan's.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人都有过类似于乔纳森的经历。

sentences.en: We suffer setbacks and failures, humiliations and disappointments.
sentences.zh: 我们遭受挫折与失败、羞辱与失望。

sentences.en: When these happen to us frequently enough, we start to think that we will never be happy, never be whole.
sentences.zh: 当这些事情频繁发生在我们身上时，我们开始认为自己永远不会快乐，永远无法完整。

sentences.en: When we come back, why unhappiness can breed unhappiness and how to break the cycle.
sentences.zh: 当我们归来时，为什么不幸会滋生不幸，以及如何打破这个循环。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Jonathan Adler spent much of his young adulthood feeling unsatisfied, yearning for more.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·阿德尔在青年时期的大部分时间里都感到不满足，渴望得到更多。

sentences.en: He sensed he was gay, but didn't feel comfortable coming out.
sentences.zh: 他隐约觉得自己是个同性恋，但对出柜感到很不自在。

sentences.en: He spent a semester in Australia to break free of the constraints of his college life in Maine,
sentences.zh: 他在澳大利亚度过了一个学期，试图摆脱他在缅因州大学生活的种种束缚，

sentences.en: but found that he was just as lonely on another continent.
sentences.zh: 却发现自己在另一个大陆上同样感到孤独。

sentences.en: Sometime after he returned to the United States, however, Jonathan made a discovery.
sentences.zh: 然而，在他回到美国后不久，乔纳森有了一个发现。

sentences.en: He came by the work of a pioneering scientist in a field known as narrative psychology.
sentences.zh: 他偶然接触到了一位被称为叙事心理学领域的先驱科学家的著作。

sentences.en: Dan McAdams at Northwestern University was arguing that the stories we tell about our lives have profound effects on our well-being.
sentences.zh: 西北大学的丹·麦克亚当斯提出，我们讲述自己人生的故事对我们的幸福感有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: Jonathan moved to Northwestern, became Dan's PhD student, and later his scientific collaborator.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森搬到了西北大学，成为了丹的博士生，后来又成为了他的科研合作者。

sentences.en: In time, Jonathan came to see his own life through the lens of his research.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，乔纳森开始通过自己研究的视角来看待他的人生。

sentences.en: He realized that he had been telling the story of his life in a way that was self-defeating.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，他一直在以一种自我挫败的方式讲述自己的人生故事。

sentences.en: And he came to see that by telling that story differently, it could make a profound difference.
sentences.zh: 并且他逐渐明白，如果以不同的方式讲述这个故事，将会产生深远的变化。

sentences.en: We'll get to that in a moment.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: First, I asked Jonathan to explain to me the basic idea behind narrative psychology.
sentences.zh: 首先，我请乔纳森向我解释叙事心理学背后的基本理念。

sentences.en: You can't totally control the things that happen to you in your life.
sentences.zh: 你无法完全控制你生活中发生的事情。

sentences.en: You have some more say about how you make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 但对于如何理解这些事情，你拥有更多的主导权。

sentences.en: And it's important to remember we're talking about stories here.
sentences.zh: 记住我们在讨论的是故事，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: So we know from research on memory that we're not very good at recording the objective facts of our experience.
sentences.zh: 从关于记忆的研究中我们知道，我们并不擅长记录经历中的客观事实。

sentences.en: For a long time, that frustrated cognitive scientists.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，这让认知科学家们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: But in more recent years, it's become clear that our memory works like this for a good reason.
sentences.zh: 但在最近几年，人们逐渐明白，我们的记忆之所以这样运作是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: So if you think about why we have memory in the first place, it's not so we can hold on to every single thing that's happened to us in some veridical way.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你思考我们为什么一开始就拥有记忆，那并不是为了让我们以某种真实的方式记住发生在自己身上的每一件事。

sentences.en: We have memories so that we can make sense of what's happening to us right now and anticipate what might happen next.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有记忆是为了让我们能够理解此时此刻正在发生的事情，并预测接下来可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: So if you walk by a cave and a bear jumps out, you don't necessarily need to remember that cave and that bear.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你走过一个山洞，突然跳出一只熊，你其实不一定非得记住那个山洞和那只熊。

sentences.en: But you need to remember that dangerous things might hide in dark places.
sentences.zh: 但你需要记住的是，危险的事物可能会藏在黑暗的地方。

sentences.en: So the slippery, reconstructive nature of memory is a feature of the system.
sentences.zh: 因此，记忆善变且具有重构性的本质是该系统的一个特征。

sentences.en: It's not a bug.
sentences.zh: 而不是一个缺陷。

sentences.en: And stories are an amazing tool for holding on to the meaning of our past experiences.
sentences.zh: 故事是保留我们过去经历意义的绝佳工具。

sentences.en: So the objective facts of our lives are what they are.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们人生的客观事实就是它们本来面目那样。

sentences.en: But the stories are about where we draw connections between things, where we parse the chapter breaks of our lives.
sentences.zh: 但故事关乎我们在哪里将事物联系起来，我们在哪里划分人生的章节断点。

sentences.en: And those are narrative acts, not historical acts.
sentences.zh: 这些都是叙事行为，而不是历史行为。

sentences.en: And the way we do that can have big implications for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做的方式会对我们的幸福感产生重大影响。

sentences.en: Jonathan and Dan McAdams have found that one of the most crucial choices we make in telling our stories,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森和丹·麦克亚当斯发现，我们在讲述自己的故事时做出的最关键的选择之一——

sentences.en: and it's important to underscore that most of us make these choices unconsciously,
sentences.zh: 需要强调的是，我们大多数人都是在无意识中做出这些选择的——

sentences.en: is where we start and stop the different chapters of our life story.
sentences.zh: 就是我们在哪里开始和结束人生故事的不同章节。

sentences.en: All lives have good and bad in it.
sentences.zh: 所有的人生中都包含好与坏。

sentences.en: And so stories that start bad and end bad don't feel great.
sentences.zh: 所以那些以糟糕开头并以糟糕结尾的故事感觉并不好。

sentences.en: And stories that start good and end good, those feel good.
sentences.zh: 而那些以美好开头并以美好结尾的故事，感觉就很棒。

sentences.en: But what we find in the research is that where we draw connections between the negative and the positive matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 但我们在研究中发现，我们在消极和积极之间建立联系的地方至关重要。

sentences.en: So stories that we narrate as starting bad and ending good, we call that a redemption sequence.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些被我们叙述为由坏变好的故事，我们称之为救赎序列。

sentences.en: And stories that start good and end bad, we call that a contamination sequence.
sentences.zh: 而那些由好变坏的故事，我们称之为污染序列。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So a redemption sequence is in some ways something bad happens to you,
sentences.zh: 所以救赎序列在某种程度上是发生了一些糟糕的事情，

sentences.en: but in some ways you're rising from the ashes, so redemption.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面你浴火重生了，这就是救赎。

sentences.en: And a contamination sequence is things are going pretty well, but then something bad happens to you,
sentences.zh: 而污染序列则是事情进展得相当顺利，但随后发生了一件糟糕的事情，

sentences.en: and then everything is downhill from there.
sentences.zh: 然后从那时起，一切都开始走下坡路了。

sentences.en: So one basically has an upward trajectory, the other one has a downward trajectory.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上一个人的人生轨迹是向上的，而另一个人的是向下的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, we're remembering these are stories, so this is how we narrate the experience,
sentences.zh: 而且再次提醒，我们要记住这些都是故事，所以这是我们叙述经历的方式，

sentences.en: not necessarily the objective facts of our lives, because all lives have good and bad.
sentences.zh: 而不一定是生活中的客观事实，因为所有人的生活都有好有坏。

sentences.en: I mean, your story about going to Australia, for example, you know, you go to Australia with high hopes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如你讲去澳大利亚的那段经历，你知道的，你带着厚望去了澳大利亚。

sentences.en: You get the starring role in a play.
sentences.zh: 你在一部戏剧里演了主角。

sentences.en: We know many people would say that's a very good thing to have happened to you.
sentences.zh: 我们知道很多人会说发生在你身上这是件大好事。

sentences.en: And then the play turns out to not be quite what was best for you,
sentences.zh: 然后结果发现这部剧并不怎么适合你，

sentences.en: or the role turns out to be not what was best for you, and you end up being very lonely.
sentences.zh: 或者说这个角色并不适合你，最后你变得非常孤独。

sentences.en: And then you can sort of see a downward sort of spiral in some ways, and in some ways it becomes a contamination story,
sentences.zh: 然后你可以在某种程度上看到一种向下的螺旋，在某种程度上它成了一个污染故事，

sentences.en: a story where something good turned bad, and then you come back to the United States,
sentences.zh: 一个好事变坏的故事，接着你回到了美国，

sentences.en: and now it feels like the bad thing that happened in Australia is with you even now,
sentences.zh: 现在感觉当年在澳大利亚发生的不幸到现在依然伴随着你，

sentences.en: and that's sort of how contamination works.
sentences.zh: 这就是污染故事的运作方式。

sentences.en: It has a contagious effect and spreads and infects other things.
sentences.zh: 它具有传染效应，会扩散并感染其他事情。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, I didn't know about Dan's work at that moment in my life,
sentences.zh: 话说回来，我人生中那个时候并不知道丹的研究，

sentences.en: so I wasn't thinking about it in storied terMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时并没有用故事的视角来看待它。

sentences.en: But indeed, I think I was living out what I can now retrospectively see was a contamination sequence.
sentences.zh: 但确实，现在回想起来，我当时正经历着我可以称之为污染序列的生活。

sentences.en: I want to talk a little bit about the effects of these sequences on our life,
sentences.zh: 我想稍微谈谈这些人生序列对我们的影响，

sentences.en: the effect of a redemption narrative and a contamination narrative.
sentences.zh: 救赎叙事和污染叙事的影响。

sentences.en: What effects do these different stories have on our lives?
sentences.zh: 这些不同的故事对我们的生活有什么影响？

sentences.en: What's the difference on our mental well-being and happiness of redemption stories versus contamination stories?
sentences.zh: 救赎故事与污染故事在我们的心理健康和幸福感方面有什么区别？

sentences.en: I have a nice short example of this from a participant in one of my earliest studies.
sentences.zh: 我从我最早的一位研究对象的经历中找到了一个很好的简短例子。

sentences.en: Briefly, this was a middle-aged man.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，这是一位中年男子。

sentences.en: He's recounting the story of the first date that he went on with the woman that he ultimately goes on to marry.
sentences.zh: 他在回忆自己和最终与之结婚的女性第一次约会的故事。

sentences.en: And the facts of the story are they go out.
sentences.zh: 故事的事实是他们一起出去了。

sentences.en: When he brings her home, they're standing on her front porch,
sentences.zh: 当他送她回家时，他们站在她家的前廊上，

sentences.en: and he leans in for a kiss, and then her dad opens the front door and interrupts them.
sentences.zh: 他凑过去想要亲吻她，然后她爸爸打开前门打断了他们。

sentences.en: So in the version that this man narrated when he shared his life story as part of participating in our research,
sentences.zh: 所以在作为我们研究对象分享自己人生故事时，这名男子叙述的版本里，

sentences.en: he frames the experience as a redemption sequence.
sentences.zh: 他将这段经历构建为一个救赎序列。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: But he might have narrated the exact same sequence of events by concluding that it was this stain on the beginning of their relationship
sentences.zh: 但他也可以通过得出这样的结论来叙述完全相同的事件序列：这是他们关系开端上的一个污点，

sentences.en: that could have contaminated the relationship in a way that they moved on from but never could erase.
sentences.zh: 这个污点本可能会污染这段关系，尽管他们后来走了出来，却永远无法抹去。

sentences.en: So neither version is more accurate in the historical sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从历史的角度来看，这两个版本并没有哪个更准确。

sentences.en: These are narrative interpretations that take on different thematic arcs, redemption and contamination.
sentences.zh: 这些是带有不同主题弧线（救赎与污染）的叙事解读。

sentences.en: But these different ways of narrating our lives have different implications for your well-being.
sentences.zh: 但这些讲述我们生活的方式对你的幸福感有着不同的影响。

sentences.en: We find over and over that when redemption sequences occur in people's life stories,
sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地发现，当人们的人生故事中出现救赎序列时，

sentences.en: they tend to be associated with positive well-being, good life satisfaction,
sentences.zh: 它们往往与积极的幸福感、良好的生活满意度相关，

sentences.en: lower levels of things like depression, higher self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 并且抑郁等负面情绪更少，自尊心更强。

sentences.en: And it's just the opposite for themes of contamination.
sentences.zh: 而对于污染主题则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So what's important here, and you've mentioned this before,
sentences.zh: 所以这里重要的一点是——你之前也提到过——

sentences.en: is that the underlying facts of the story don't have to change for the story, in fact, to be a very different kind of story.
sentences.zh: 为了让故事成为一种截然不同类型的故事，故事底层的基本事实甚至不需要改变。

sentences.en: So, for example, in your own life, you're still a gay man coming of age at a time when homophobia is rampant.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，在你自己的生活中，你依然是一个在恐同现象猖獗的时代长大的男同性恋。

sentences.en: You're still lonely in college.
sentences.zh: 你在大学里依然感到孤独。

sentences.en: The Australia trip was less of an escape and more of a setback.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚之行与其说是逃离，不如说是一个挫折。

sentences.en: But you can tell both a contamination story as well as a redemption story built around those facts.
sentences.zh: 但你完全可以围绕这些事实，既讲出一个污染故事，也能讲出一个救赎故事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, the shift there is about where we draw the chapter breaks in my life.
sentences.zh: 而且再次说明，这里的转变在于我们在我人生的哪个地方画下了章节的断点。

sentences.en: So if we end that story, end that chapter, when I get back to college,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们把那个故事、那个章节结束在我回到大学的时候，

sentences.en: it feels like a contamination sequence.
sentences.zh: 它感觉就像一个污染序列。

sentences.en: But if I string it together with the things that came next, spoiler alert, it feels like a redemption sequence.
sentences.zh: 但如果我把它和接下来发生的事情串联起来——剧透一下——它感觉就像一个救赎序列。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened next and how it becomes a redemption story.
sentences.zh: 告诉我接下来发生了什么，以及它是如何变成一个救赎故事的。

sentences.en: As I neared the end of college, I largely dealt with my internal turmoil by just throwing myself into my work.
sentences.zh: 随着大学生活接近尾声，我基本上是通过全身心投入工作来应对内心的混乱。

sentences.en: So I was one of the top students in my class, and I got some awards, and I took a research job after college at Harvard,
sentences.zh: 所以我是班里名列前茅的学生之一，我得了一些奖项，大学毕业后我在哈佛找到了一份研究工作，

sentences.en: which was, you know, my plan was going to graduate school.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的计划是去读研究生。

sentences.en: And I felt like I had done everything expected of me, and I didn't really seek out any mentorship
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己完成了别人对我的所有期望，而且我也没有真正寻求任何导师的指导，

sentences.en: as I applied to 10 very competitive PhD prograMs.
sentences.zh: 当时我申请了10个竞争非常激烈的博士项目。

sentences.en: And then when the whole process was done, I only got into one program.
sentences.zh: 结果整个流程下来，我只被一个项目录取了。

sentences.en: So I always tell students, you only go to one school, so it only takes one.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是告诉学生，你只能去一所学校，所以有一个就够了。

sentences.en: And that is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But at the time, it felt like a shock.
sentences.zh: 但当时，这感觉像是一个打击。

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong, I was actually really excited by the one option in front of me.
sentences.zh: 别误会，其实我对摆在面前的这唯一选择感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: But I had sort of imagined that I might have more choice when approaching this next big chapter of my life.
sentences.zh: 但我原本想象着在迈向人生下一个大篇章时，自己可能会有更多选择。

sentences.en: And as you said, the one school I got into was in the Midwest, a place that I had never been for more than a few days.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我被录取的唯一一所学校在中西部，一个我从未呆过超过几天的地方。

sentences.en: And so I was thinking a lot about what it would mean to be a gay man living in this different part of the country than I was used to.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想了很多，作为一个男同性恋，生活在一个与我习惯的地区不同的地方意味着什么。

sentences.en: So how does this become a redemption story?
sentences.zh: 那么，这怎么就成了一个救赎故事呢？

sentences.en: I'm still, it sounds actually the contamination is getting worse here because you apply to all these colleges and you don't get into them.
sentences.zh: 听起来污染似乎还在恶化，因为你申请了所有这些大学却都没被录取。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So here's what happened.
sentences.zh: 所以事情是这样的。

sentences.en: So I went to campus for my interview, and it was spring break week.
sentences.zh: 我为了面试去了校园，正好赶上春假周。

sentences.en: So no one was really around.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上没什么人在。

sentences.en: But after the formal stuff was done, I sort of casually walked by the LGBT student group's office.
sentences.zh: 但正事办完后，我顺便溜达着路过了LGBT学生组织的办公室。

sentences.en: And there was this little yellow envelope of business cards tacked to the bulletin board outside that said something like,
sentences.zh: 外面的公告栏上钉着一个小小的黄色名片信封，上面写着类似这样的话：

sentences.en: questions?
sentences.zh: 有问题吗？

sentences.en: Email us at, and then, you know, some generic email address.
sentences.zh: 发邮件给我们，然后你知道的，是一个通用邮箱地址。

sentences.en: So when I got home, I sent this email saying, I'm thinking of coming here for graduate school.
sentences.zh: 所以回家后，我发了封邮件说：我考虑来这里读研究生。

sentences.en: I've never lived in the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 我从来没在中西部住过。

sentences.en: What's it like to be there and be a gay person, both on campus and in the surrounding community?
sentences.zh: 无论是校园里还是周围社区，在那里生活是怎样的体验？

sentences.en: And we didn't even have internet at the house that I was renting with some friends.
sentences.zh: 我和几个朋友租的房子里甚至连互联网都没有。

sentences.en: So I had to sneak into the computer lab at the nearby college to check my email.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不溜进附近学院的计算机实验室去查收邮件。

sentences.en: So a few days later, I got a perfectly nice and very thorough email reassuring me from a senior undergrad about what it was like to go to school there and live in the town.
sentences.zh: 几天后，我收到了一封来自一位高年级本科生的非常友好且详尽的邮件，他安慰了我，并向我介绍了在那里上学和在镇上生活的感受。

sentences.en: And I'm sure it was a copy and paste of an email that he had sent many times before.
sentences.zh: 我确信这一定是他以前复制粘贴过很多次的邮件内容。

sentences.en: But I appreciated how clear it was and the bits of humor sprinkled in.
sentences.zh: 但我很感激它的清晰明了，以及字里行间点缀的一点点幽默。

sentences.en: And I wrote back to say, you know, thanks.
sentences.zh: 我回信说，谢谢你。

sentences.en: That was so super helpful.
sentences.zh: 这真的是超级有帮助。

sentences.en: And then this student said, I'm actually graduating early, but I'm going to be hanging around.
sentences.zh: 然后这个学生说，其实我快提前毕业了，但我还会在这里待一阵子。

sentences.en: I'm handing off the listserv.
sentences.zh: 我要把邮件列表交接出去。

sentences.en: But if you have questions, you know, just send me an email.
sentences.zh: 不过如果你有问题，你知道的，尽管发邮件给我。

sentences.en: And so quite a bit of time goes by.
sentences.zh: 于是过了相当长一段时间。

sentences.en: And I did commit to going to school there.
sentences.zh: 我确实决定去那里上学了。

sentences.en: And when it was time for me to start looking for an apartment, I reached out again.
sentences.zh: 当我要开始找公寓时，我又联系了他。

sentences.en: And more than 20 years later, we are now married and have two kids and a dog.
sentences.zh: 20多年后的今天，我们已经结婚了，还有两个孩子和一只狗。

sentences.en: So those first emails weren't even remotely flirty, but they were attuned and connected and kind and funny.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的那些邮件甚至连调情的边都沾不上，但它们细心、紧密相连、善良且有趣。

sentences.en: And eventually they did get flirty, as did my responses.
sentences.zh: 最终它们确实变得带有调情意味了，我的回复也是如此。

sentences.en: And so I look back at this turning point in my life with a profound sense of, first of all, gratitude, but also redemption, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，当我回首人生中的这个转折点时，首先涌现出的是一种深深的感激之情，当然，还有救赎，对吧？

sentences.en: What at the time felt like close to failure, right?
sentences.zh: 当时感觉几乎是彻底失败的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: That all my work in college and all my ignoring of my personal life for the sake of my intellectual life had presented me with only one option.
sentences.zh: 为了知识生活而付出的所有大学学业以及对个人生活的忽视，最终只让我得到了一个选择。

sentences.en: Now feels like the universe trying to make sure that I found my way.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉就像是宇宙在努力确保我找到属于自己的路。

sentences.en: And within a year, I was having a more gratifying intellectual experience than I had ever imagined.
sentences.zh: 不到一年的时间里，我获得的学术体验比我以往想象的还要充实满意。

sentences.en: And I was in love.
sentences.zh: 而且我坠入爱河了。

sentences.en: I'm wondering in some ways if the narrative changing played some role in sort of these things happening in your life.
sentences.zh: 我在想，在某种程度上，叙事的转变是否在这些发生在你生活中的事情中发挥了一定作用？

sentences.en: Is it just that you had a series of bad luck and bad events happening to you?
sentences.zh: 难道只是因为你接连遭遇了倒霉事和坏运气？

sentences.en: And then you had a series of good luck and good events happening to you?
sentences.zh: 然后你又接连遇到了好运气和好事？

sentences.en: I mean, that might be the case, but that's not particularly, you know, interesting from a psychological point of view.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许确实如此，但从心理学的角度来看，这并没有什么特别有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Do you think that the way you were thinking about your own life and your exposure to Dan's ideas had reshaped your ability or your willingness to be open to thinking about a relationship in a different way or thinking about flirting on email with someone?
sentences.zh: 你是否认为，你思考自己生活的方式以及你接触到丹的理念，重塑了你开放思考一段不同关系的能力或意愿，或者改变了你愿意通过邮件与某人调情的态度？

sentences.en: Yeah, I really appreciate you bringing that up because, indeed, one could say, well, the objective facts were things were bad and then things were good.
sentences.zh: 是的，我非常感谢你提出这一点，因为确实，有人可能会说，客观事实就是事情先变糟然后又变好了。

sentences.en: It really matters where we draw the chapter breaks in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中划定章节断点的位置真的很重要。

sentences.en: So, yeah, one could say, well, that horrible chapter is over and this new chapter is just a good chapter.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有人可能会说，哦，那段糟糕的章节结束了，这个新章节纯粹是个好章节。

sentences.en: But I actually think it is the way I have woven those two experiences together in my life story where it feels like redemption.

sentences.en: So to pan back for just a second, when we think about the broad study of well-being,
sentences.zh: 退一步来讲，当我们思考关于幸福的广泛研究时，

sentences.en: it tends to cluster in sort of two domains, which get their cumbersome names from Aristotle.

sentences.en: So on the one hand, we have what's called hedonic well-being, which means it feels good.

sentences.en: And on the other hand, we have a kind of well-being called eudaimonic well-being,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们有一种被称为“实现型幸福”（eudaimonic well-being）的幸福，

sentences.en: which means it feels meaningful.
sentences.zh: 意思是感觉有意义。

sentences.en: And these two domains of well-being are actually relatively uncorrelated with each other.
sentences.zh: 而这两个幸福领域实际上彼此之间并没有太大关联。

sentences.en: And if we think about our lives for a second, that makes sense, right?

sentences.en: And we can all think about experiences that feel meaningful, but don't feel particularly good.

sentences.en: So in my work with Health Story Collaborative in particular, we find that feeling good is not always an option for people.

sentences.en: Telling redemptive stories or stories high in the theme of agency and communion, that's not always possible.

sentences.en: And in those situations, we're often interested in the ways in which people can really think through the hard parts of their lives and find some meaning out of that.

sentences.en: And even if the meaning doesn't ultimately feel good in that sort of happy sense, that meaning is still incredibly worthwhile.

sentences.en: I'm trying to imagine how someone who is going through a rough time might hear this episode, Jonathan.

sentences.zh: 我刚刚失去了亲密的家庭朋友。

sentences.en: Of course, they're hard.
sentences.zh: 这是当然的，生活确实很难。

sentences.en: And of course, you're not feeling good.
sentences.zh: 你感觉不好也是理所当然的。

sentences.en: The second thing I want to say is there are all kinds of ways of making meaning of these experiences.
sentences.zh: 我想说的第二件事是，有各种各样的方式来赋予这些经历以意义。

sentences.en: And so we might think about exploring themes of agency or communion.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以考虑探索自主或共融的主题。

sentences.en: So if you lost your job, are you feeling connected to your spouse or your kids?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你失业了，你是否感到了与配偶或孩子的联系？

sentences.en: Or, you know, if something challenging has happened, might there be some growth that comes from it?
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，如果发生了充满挑战的事情，其中是否可能会带来某种成长？

sentences.en: So we might explore those themes.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以探索这些主题。

sentences.en: But the third thing I want to say is our personal stories exist in a broader narrative ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的第三件事是，我们的个人故事存在于一个更广阔的叙事生态系统中。

sentences.en: And in the United States, there is an expectation that we can narrate challenging experiences in our lives with a redemptive spin.
sentences.zh: 在美国，有一种期望，即我们能够以带有救赎色彩的方式来讲述生活中的挑战性经历。

sentences.en: We Americans love the theme of redemption, and we expect people to be able to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们美国人热爱救赎的主题，并且期望人们能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I call this the press for redemption.
sentences.zh: 我把这称为对救赎的催促（the press for redemption）。

sentences.en: And in my work with Health Story Collaborative, we often find that people feel like they're having this double whammy experience where, you know,
sentences.zh: 在我与健康故事协作组织的工作中，我们经常发现人们感觉自己经历了双重打击，你知道的，

sentences.en: I'm sick and I'm not telling the right kind of story about it.
sentences.zh: 我生病了，但我却没有讲述关于它的正确故事。

sentences.en: So my cancer didn't teach me that I'm such a fighter or that people love me more than I ever would have realized if I never had cancer.
sentences.zh: 所以我的癌症并没有教会我我是个多么坚强的斗士，也没有让我觉得人们比我得癌症前更加爱我。

sentences.en: No, some people say, you know, this just sucks.
sentences.zh: 不，有些人会说，你知道，这简直糟透了。

sentences.en: And I think in those instances, we want to acknowledge that and not try to convince them that it doesn't just suck.
sentences.zh: 我认为在那些情况下，我们应该承认这一点，而不是试图去说服他们这其实并不糟透了。

sentences.en: Let them know that there's a reason they feel like they're telling the wrong kind of story because our culture puts a particular premium on a particular kind of story.
sentences.zh: 让他们知道，他们觉得自己讲错了故事是有原因的，因为我们的文化对某种特定类型的故事赋予了极高的价值。

sentences.en: And then to help them find other kinds of narrative roots that might lead towards a sense of meaningfulness, even if they can't make you feel better.
sentences.zh: 然后帮助他们找到其他可能通往意义感的叙事根基，即使这些根基并不能让你感觉更好。

sentences.en: So many of the examples we've talked about here have involved individuals.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里讨论的许多例子都涉及个体。

sentences.en: But as we've started to see, I think, towards the end of this conversation, we're slowly broadening out beyond the individual because, of course,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们开始看到的，我认为在这场对话的尾声，我们正在慢慢超越个体，因为当然，

sentences.en: these ideas are relevant outside of individual minds as well.
sentences.zh: 这些理念在个体心智之外也同样具有现实意义。

sentences.en: So societies tell themselves narratives.
sentences.zh: 所以，社会也会对自己讲述叙事。

sentences.en: Nations tell themselves stories all the time.
sentences.zh: 国家无时无刻不在对自己讲述故事。

sentences.en: Do you think ideas of narrative psychology speak to how nations talk to themselves and perhaps how they ought to talk to themselves?
sentences.zh: 你认为叙事心理学的理念是否能够解释国家是如何对自己说话的，以及它们或许应当如何对自己说话？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is really at the forefront of the field.
sentences.zh: 这确实是该领域的前沿课题。

sentences.en: So my colleagues, Kate McLean and Moin Syed, have written really compellingly about what they call master narratives.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的同事凯特·麦克莱恩（Kate McLean）和莫因·赛义德（Moin Syed）就他们所谓的“主导叙事”（master narratives）撰写了极具说服力的文章。

sentences.en: So these are the dominant storylines in our culture that tend to be invisible, but also ubiquitous and sort of rigid and powerful.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们文化中占主导地位的故事线，它们往往无形却又无处不在，且带有一种刚性和力量。

sentences.en: And we are always in a constant dialogue with the master narratives in our particular cultural contexts.
sentences.zh: 我们始终与特定文化语境中的主导叙事进行着持续的对话。

sentences.en: You know, families have narratives that guide the way relationships unfold.
sentences.zh: 你知道，家庭也有指导关系发展的叙事。

sentences.en: And as you said, countries certainly do.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，国家当然也有。

sentences.en: So, again, narratives are not all good or all bad at the individual level, and they're not all good or all bad at the national level either.
sentences.zh: 因此，再次说明，叙事在个人层面并非全好或全坏，在国家层面同样如此。

sentences.en: But these national narratives are emergent from the collection of individual narratives that the members of that country tell.
sentences.zh: 但这些国家叙事是从该国成员所讲述的个人叙事的集合中涌现出来的。

sentences.en: So a number of years ago, Jonathan, when you were still living in Illinois, the junior senator from your state gave a memorable speech at the 2004 Democratic National Convention.
sentences.zh: 所以多年前，乔纳森，当你还住在伊利诺伊州时，你州的年轻参议员在2004年民主党全国代表大会上发表了一场难忘的演讲。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the speech that first put Barack Obama in the national spotlight.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段这段演讲的剪辑，正是这段演讲让巴拉克·奥巴马首次成为全国瞩目的焦点。

sentences.en: I'm not talking about blind optimism here.
sentences.zh: 我这里说的不是盲目的乐观。

sentences.en: The almost willful ignorance that thinks unemployment will go away if we just don't think about it,
sentences.zh: 那种近乎执拗的无知，以为只要我们不去想，失业率就会消失，

sentences.en: or health care crisis will solve itself if we just ignore it.
sentences.zh: 或者只要我们无视它，医疗保健危机就会自行解决。

sentences.en: That's not what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 这不是我在谈论的。

sentences.en: I'm talking about something more substantial.
sentences.zh: 我在谈论更实质性的东西。

sentences.en: It's the hope of slaves sitting around a fire singing freedom songs.
sentences.zh: 那是奴隶们围坐在火堆旁唱着自由之歌的希望。

sentences.en: The hope of immigrants setting out for distant shores.
sentences.zh: 是移民们启程前往遥远彼岸的希望。

sentences.en: The hope of a young naval lieutenant bravely patrolling the Mekong Delta.
sentences.zh: 是一名年轻海军中尉勇敢巡逻湄公河三角洲的希望。

sentences.en: The hope of a mill worker's son who dares to defy the odds.
sentences.zh: 是一个磨坊工人的儿子敢于向命运抗争的希望。

sentences.en: The hope of a skinny kid with a funny name who believes that America has a place for him too.
sentences.zh: 是一个名字滑稽的瘦弱男孩，坚信美国也有一席之地的希望。

sentences.en: Hope.
sentences.zh: 希望。

sentences.en: Hope in the face of difficulty.
sentences.zh: 面对艰难险阻时的希望。

sentences.en: Hope in the face of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 面对未卜前途时的希望。

sentences.en: The audacity of hope.
sentences.zh: 希望的无畏力量（The audacity of hope）。

sentences.en: In the end, that is God's greatest gift to us.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，那是上帝赐予我们的最伟大礼物。

sentences.en: The bedrock of this nation.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的基石。

sentences.en: A belief in things not seen.
sentences.zh: 对未见之事的信念。

sentences.en: A belief that there are better days ahead.
sentences.zh: 对美好未来终将到来的信念。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Jonathan, as someone who has studied narrative psychology for a number of years,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，作为一个研究叙事心理学多年的人，我想知道，

sentences.en: how do you hear that speech?
sentences.zh: 你是如何看待那场演讲的？

sentences.en: So then Senator Obama was tapping into the American master narrative of redemption.
sentences.zh: 当时的参议员奥巴马正在汲取美国关于救赎的主导叙事。

sentences.en: Each of those images includes this shift from negative to positive.
sentences.zh: 这些意象中的每一个都包含了从消极到积极的转变。

sentences.en: And, you know, like all political speeches, this was a strategic communication with very particular aims
sentences.zh: 你知道，像所有政治演讲一样，这是一次战略沟通，有着非常明确的目的，

sentences.en: focused on stirring the public to support this speaker's preferred candidates and issues.
sentences.zh: 旨在激发公众去支持演讲者青睐的候选人和议题。

sentences.en: So appealing to entrenched master narratives is a very strategic thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，呼吁根深蒂固的主导叙事是一种极具战略意义的做法。

sentences.en: And many, many politicians adopt redemptive themes in their speeches.
sentences.zh: 许许多多的政治家都在他们的演讲中采用了救赎的主题。

sentences.en: And obviously there are many wonderful aspects of that storyline.
sentences.zh: 显然，那个故事线有许多精彩的方面。

sentences.en: And as we've discussed, problematic ones too.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，也有充满问题的一面。

sentences.en: But we see evidence of leaders serving as narrators in chief.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到领导人充当首席叙事者的证据。

sentences.en: They shape our narrative ecology as they model storytelling for us.
sentences.zh: 他们在为我们塑造故事模型的同时，也在塑造我们的叙事生态。

sentences.en: We started this conversation, Jonathan, by talking about ways in which you came to understand
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们这场对话的开始，是讨论你如何开始理解

sentences.en: the life events in your own life and to tell stories about those life events
sentences.zh: 你生命中的生活事件，并以一种

sentences.en: in a way that was more positive than negative.
sentences.zh: 由消极转为积极的方式来讲述这些生活事件。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, after all these years of studying narrative psychology, do you do this on a regular
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在研究了多年的叙事心理学之后，你现在是否会定期这样做

sentences.en: basis now?
sentences.zh: 呢？

sentences.en: What are the stories you tell yourself today in terms of where you are and where your life
sentences.zh: 就你目前的生活状态以及你的人生

sentences.en: is and where you want your life to go?
sentences.zh: 现状如何，你又希望你的人生去往何方？

sentences.en: So it's not that I am consciously going through my daily experiences and editing them into the
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我有意在日常经历中去穿针引线，

sentences.en: kinds of storylines that I have learned are likely to support my well-being.
sentences.zh: 把它们编辑成那些我深知有助于提升幸福感的故事情节。

sentences.en: But when difficult things happen in particular, I think I do pause and I remember that there
sentences.zh: 但每当遇到困难时，我想我确实会停下来，提醒自己

sentences.en: are different kinds of well-being and that the way I make sense of those experiences will
sentences.zh: 幸福其实有不同的种类，我如何解读这些经历，

sentences.en: lead me to different kinds of well-being.
sentences.zh: 将引导我走向不同种类的幸福。

sentences.en: But I think for a lot of people, just the awareness that you are not only the main character in your
sentences.zh: 但我想对许多人来说，仅仅意识到你不仅是故事里的主角，

sentences.en: story, but also the narrator and that the way you choose to tell the story of your life really
sentences.zh: 同时也是叙述者，而你选择讲述自己人生故事的方式至关重要，

sentences.en: matters, that can be an empowering insight.
sentences.zh: 这种洞察会让人感到充满力量。

sentences.en: Jonathan Adler is a psychologist at Olin College.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·阿德勒是欧林学院的一位心理学家。

sentences.zh: 乔纳森，非常感谢你今天来到《隐性大脑》。。

sentences.en: Oh, it's been an incredible pleasure.
sentences.zh: 哦，这真是莫大的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: For today's Unsung Hero, we bring you a story from our sister show, My Unsung Hero.
sentences.zh: 在今天的“无名英雄”环节，我们为你带来姊妹节目《我心中的无名英雄》里的一个故事。

sentences.en: The story comes from listener Rich Addison.
sentences.zh: 这个故事来自听众里奇·艾迪森。

sentences.en: So when I was young, I was very shy.
sentences.zh: 所以当我年轻的时候，我非常害羞。

sentences.en: I was an only child who was pretty comfortable talking to adults, but I never had any brothers
sentences.zh: 我是个独生子女，和成年人聊天时挺自在的，但我从来没有

sentences.en: and sisters to practice on, so I wasn't very good at kind of mixing it up with the other
sentences.zh: 兄弟姐妹可以拿来练习，所以我很不善于跟其他

sentences.en: kids.
sentences.zh: 孩子们打成一片。

sentences.en: And I remember being very anxious about going to school.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己对去学校感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: And on Sunday nights, I would not be able to sleep, just worrying about what would happen
sentences.zh: 每到周日晚上，我就会急得睡不着觉，总是担心和其他

sentences.en: with the other kids.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在一起时会发生什么。

sentences.en: So now, flash forward a few years, and I'm in high school, and I realized that I had to
sentences.zh: 现在时间快进几年，我上了高中，我意识到

sentences.en: be different, that I couldn't keep being so shy.
sentences.zh: 我必须改变，不能再这么害羞下去了。

sentences.en: So I went about developing a quick wit and a sense of humor that would keep other kids
sentences.zh: 于是我开始培养一种敏捷的机智和幽默感，好让其他孩子

sentences.en: off balance so I wouldn't have to feel powerless.
sentences.zh: 摸不着头脑，这样我就不用感到无能为力了。

sentences.en: You know how sometimes people say the best defense is a good offense?
sentences.zh: 你知道人们有时会说“最好的防守就是进攻”吗？

sentences.en: Well, that was what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时就是在这样做。

sentences.en: But the sense of humor I developed was kind of biting and kind of critical.
sentences.zh: 但我培养出的幽默感有点尖酸刻薄，而且爱批评人。

sentences.en: So now, my hero is about to come into the story.
sentences.zh: 好了，我的故事里的英雄马上就要登场了。

sentences.en: And this was my friend Holly.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的朋友霍莉。

sentences.en: And one day, Holly and I were talking, and she said to me, you know, Rich, sometimes you
sentences.zh: 有一天，我和霍莉在聊天，她对我说，你知道吗，里奇，有时你

sentences.en: really hurt people's feelings.
sentences.zh: 真的会伤害别人的感情。

sentences.en: And at first, I was just shocked.
sentences.zh: 起初，我简直震惊了。

sentences.en: I said to myself, that can't be true.
sentences.zh: 我心想，这绝不可能。

sentences.en: I was entertaining.
sentences.zh: 我很有趣啊。

sentences.en: I made people laugh.
sentences.zh: 我逗笑过大家。

sentences.en: I liked people.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢别人。

sentences.en: These were my friends.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我的朋友。

sentences.en: I didn't want to hurt them.
sentences.zh: 我并不想伤害他们。

sentences.en: I couldn't be hurting them.
sentences.zh: 我不可能在伤害他们。

sentences.en: But I kept thinking about what Holly said, and I kept turning it over in my mind.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在琢磨霍莉的话，在脑海里反复思量。

sentences.en: And eventually, I realized that she was absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 最终，我意识到她完全说对了。

sentences.en: And I started paying attention to how my humor was affecting other people.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意我的幽默是如何影响其他人的。

sentences.en: And I changed it.
sentences.zh: 我做出了改变。

sentences.en: And it didn't happen immediately.
sentences.zh: 这并不是立竿见影的。

sentences.en: It didn't happen overnight.
sentences.zh: 也不是一夜之间发生的。

sentences.en: But I changed.
sentences.zh: 但我确实变了。

sentences.en: And I wanted to be more compassionate towards people.
sentences.zh: 我希望能对他人多一些悲悯之心。

sentences.en: And I wanted to have a different kind of relationship with them than always keeping them off balance.
sentences.zh: 我希望与他们建立一种不同的关系，而不是总让他们摸不透、心里没底。

sentences.en: So, after I went on to become a clinical psychologist, and in my role, I try to help other people have generous interpretations about themselves and others.
sentences.zh: 后来，我成了一名临床心理学家，在我的工作中，我努力帮助他人对自己和他人产生宽容的解读。

sentences.en: And I've also made a career out of training physicians to do that.
sentences.zh: 我还把培训医生做这件事当成了我的职业。

sentences.en: And I really am so grateful that I made that shift in my life.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激自己当年在生活中做出了那样的转变。

sentences.en: And I really owe it to Holly.
sentences.zh: 我真的要好好感谢霍莉。

sentences.en: And I think back to that time so many years ago, and when she cared enough to say something to me, something that probably wasn't easy to say,
sentences.zh: 每当回想起那么多年前的那段时光，她居然那么在乎，对我说出了那些话——那些或许并不容易说出口的话，

sentences.en: but it was something that changed the direction of my life in a very significant and very gratifying way.
sentences.zh: 但正是那些话，以一种极其深刻且令人欣慰的方式改变了我人生的方向。

sentences.en: So, thank you, Holly.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你，霍莉。

sentences.en: You're my unsung hero.
sentences.zh: 你是我心中的无名英雄。

sentences.zh: 里奇·艾迪森住在加利福尼亚州圣罗莎。

sentences.zh: 最近，他得以重新联系上霍莉，并告诉她，在大约 50 年后，她当年的那句话对他的意义有多重大。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 我们回头见。
